25 Which list shows electromagnetic waves in order of decreasing frequency?
A
gamma-rays  infrared  ultraviolet  radio waves
B
gamma-rays  ultraviolet  infrared  radio waves
C
radio waves  infrared  ultraviolet  gamma-rays
D
radio waves  ultraviolet  infrared  gamma-rays

hints: Notice the question asks for decreasing frequency, so the first wave in the list must have the highest $f$ and shortest wavelength - think whether gamma-rays or radio waves fit there.
Recall $c = f\lambda$ for all EM waves, so higher frequency means shorter wavelength. Gamma-rays are at the high-$f$ end and radio waves at the low-$f$ end.
Focus on the middle pair infrared and ultraviolet around visible light. Ultraviolet is beyond violet with higher $f$ than visible, while infrared is beyond red with lower $f$ than visible.
walkthrough: Recall the full EM spectrum in order of decreasing frequency: gamma-rays, X-rays, ultraviolet, visible, infrared, microwaves, radio waves.
Decreasing frequency means start with the largest $f$ and shortest wavelength and move to the smallest $f$ and longest wavelength, since $c = f\lambda$ with $c$ constant.
Of the waves listed, gamma-rays have the highest frequency and radio waves have the lowest frequency, so any decreasing list must start with gamma-rays and end with radio waves.
Between the middle two, ultraviolet has higher frequency than visible light and infrared has lower frequency than visible light, so ultraviolet comes before infrared in decreasing $f$.
Putting this together gives gamma-rays $\rightarrow$ ultraviolet $\rightarrow$ infrared $\rightarrow$ radio waves. This is option B.

A.explanation: Infrared does not have higher frequency than ultraviolet. Ultraviolet is closer to gamma-rays with higher $f$ and shorter wavelength than infrared.

B.explanation: Frequency decreases from gamma-rays to ultraviolet to infrared to radio waves, matching the EM spectrum order of decreasing $f$.

C.explanation: This is increasing frequency, not decreasing. Radio waves have the lowest frequency and gamma-rays have the highest frequency.

D.explanation: It starts with the lowest frequency and ends with the highest, and also swaps infrared and ultraviolet. Ultraviolet has higher frequency than infrared.
